evidence.claim: After the recall vote, AMLO said more than 90% supported his continuing mandate, described the exercise as a step for democracy, and reiterated that he would not govern beyond September 2024.
evidence.title: Más de 90% de votantes quieren que el presidente de la República continúe su mandato
evidence.publisher: Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 | Gobierno | gob.mx
evidence.excerpt: After the recall vote, AMLO said more than 90% supported his continuing mandate, described the exercise as a step for democracy, and reiterated that he would not govern beyond September 2024.
evidence.source_locator: official press statement / closing paragraphs of the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government statement by the ruler himself, directly attributable on dates and intent, though self-serving on effects.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period evidence on contestability and succession signaling.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO speech as president; fully attributable as his own public position, though not proof of implementation.
contrary_evidence: A recall vote is not the same as a free competitive election, and the statement does not by itself prove broad respect for independent institutions.

evidence.claim: AFP found that a circulated video suggesting AMLO proposed extending his mandate was edited; the full remarks show he rejected staying in office beyond September 30, 2024.
evidence.title: Este video en el que AMLO habla de ampliar su mandato fue editado; él rechaza esa posibilidad
evidence.excerpt: AFP found that a circulated video suggesting AMLO proposed extending his mandate was edited; the full remarks show he rejected staying in office beyond September 30, 2024.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent fact-check built around the transcript and the original public remarks; strong for the no-extension claim.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence about term-limit signaling during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public statements; useful for intention, not a legal safeguard by itself.
contrary_evidence: It is evidence of stated restraint, not a completed transfer of power or a tested refusal under real succession pressure.

evidence.claim: Mexico's lower house rejected a president-backed electoral reform that critics said could undermine electoral independence; the bill sought to make the National Electoral Institute smaller and more politically controlled, and AMLO immediately pursued an alternate route requiring only a simple majority.
evidence.title: Mexican Congress rejects president's electoral reform bid
evidence.excerpt: Mexico's lower house rejected a president-backed electoral reform that critics said could undermine electoral independence; the bill sought to make the National Electoral Institute smaller and more politically controlled, and AMLO immediately pursued an alternate route requiring only a simple majority.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete legislative episode with named vote counts and direct attribution to the president's reform effort.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 target-period legislative action by the ruler and his coalition.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the reform was backed by AMLO and the article describes his immediate follow-on strategy.
contrary_evidence: AMLO defended the proposal as strengthening democracy and reducing the influence of economic interests in politics.
Congress, not AMLO alone, blocked the constitutional version.

evidence.claim: Tens of thousands protested AMLO's electoral reform plan in Mexico City, saying they feared it would concentrate power in the hands of the government.
evidence.title: Tens of thousands protest Mexican president's electoral reform plan
evidence.excerpt: Tens of thousands protested AMLO's electoral reform plan in Mexico City, saying they feared it would concentrate power in the hands of the government.
evidence.source_locator: story summary / Reuters archive licensing record
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters archive summary is clear on the event and public reaction, though it is a compressed secondary record rather than the full article.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 protest against a ruler-sponsored political reform.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The protest was against AMLO's own reform plan, so the attribution to his conduct is direct, though the protest itself is not proof of coercion.
contrary_evidence: Mass protest also shows active civic resistance and did not itself prove state repression.
The summary alone does not document the government's immediate response.

evidence.claim: The country page says the Mexican news industry contends with the president's daily attacks on its credibility, that AMLO's morning briefings became more pointed with a 'Who's Who' segment targeting journalists and publications, and that journalists continued to be murdered in 2022.
evidence.title: Mexico
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: The country page says the Mexican news industry contends with the president's daily attacks on its credibility, that AMLO's morning briefings became more pointed with a 'Who's Who' segment targeting journalists and publications, and that journalists continued to be murdered in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A reputable annual country analysis from the Reuters Institute synthesizing the 2022 information environment and press climate.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 press-environment evidence, though some homicide figures are cumulative/contextual.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to AMLO's daily briefings and public messaging; journalist killings themselves are mostly context and not wholly ruler-caused.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that murders were often linked to organized crime, so not every press killing can be attributed to the president.
Mexico still had active independent media and visible public criticism.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that AMLO said his government would channel a quarter of its publicity budget into health insurance and pensions for poorer journalists, while noting the move could affect traditional media revenues and reflected a fractious relationship with critical outlets.
evidence.title: Mexico's president, a fierce press critic, offers benefits to journalists
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that AMLO said his government would channel a quarter of its publicity budget into health insurance and pensions for poorer journalists, while noting the move could affect traditional media revenues and reflected a fractious relationship with critical outlets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete public-policy announcement, with useful context about press relations and likely side effects.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy and rhetoric on the media environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO as a government action; the press-effect analysis is interpretive but tied to his announcement.
contrary_evidence: This could be read as welfare support for precarious journalists rather than pure coercion.
The article itself notes a possible revenue hit to traditional media, so the measure is mixed rather than clearly protective.

evidence.claim: ARTICLE 19 condemned AMLO's morning conference attack on Carlos Loret de Mola, saying the president denigrated and criminalized the journalist by exposing alleged income data in a way that was intimidating and violated press freedom and privacy standards.
evidence.title: Ejecutivo Federal abusa del poder público para estigmatizar a la prensa
evidence.excerpt: ARTICLE 19 condemned AMLO's morning conference attack on Carlos Loret de Mola, saying the president denigrated and criminalized the journalist by exposing alleged income data in a way that was intimidating and violated press freedom and privacy standards.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous rights-organization statement describing a specific ruler-attributed press incident.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 incident in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO because the complaint concerns his own public conference and remarks.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue it was criticizing alleged false reporting rather than suppressing journalism.
The article is advocacy-oriented, so the precise legal characterization is stronger than the normative conclusion.

evidence.claim: The report says independent media often self-censored due to fear of reprisals, that politicians including President López Obrador publicly discredited journalists as biased or corrupt, and that the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment worsened official discrediting of press workers.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Mexico
evidence.excerpt: The report says independent media often self-censored due to fear of reprisals, that politicians including President López Obrador publicly discredited journalists as biased or corrupt, and that the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment worsened official discrediting of press workers.
evidence.source_locator: lines 139-140 and 237-239, plus executive summary context
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual government human-rights report with direct factual descriptions of the 2022 press environment and state treatment of journalists.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022; strong because it directly reports the target year's conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: AMLO-specific in the sense that the report names him as a discrediting actor and ties the media segment to his morning conference; other pressures are broader context.
contrary_evidence: The report also says the government generally respected free expression and that independent media remained active.
Some intimidation came from criminal groups, not only the president or his administration.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said police violently and disproportionately repressed a peaceful student protest, used racist, classist and misogynistic insults, detained 93 people, and that the abuses remained unpunished a year later, illustrating a continuing threat to protest rights in Mexico.
evidence.title: The right to protest is under threat in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said police violently and disproportionately repressed a peaceful student protest, used racist, classist and misogynistic insults, detained 93 people, and that the abuses remained unpunished a year later, illustrating a continuing threat to protest rights in Mexico.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous rights reporting with named incident, victims, and remedy failure, though the core incident occurred in 2021.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2021 incident published in 2022; useful for the 2022 pattern and aftermath, not a fresh 2022 crackdown order.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The episode is attributed to state police under the national political environment; direct federal command is weaker than for the presidential press or electoral reforms.
contrary_evidence: The incident predates the publication year, so it is better evidence of 2022 aftermath and pattern than of a new 2022 decision.
The article focuses on one state-level episode, not a full nationwide repression system.

unresolved_gaps: Federal command attribution is still thin for several state-level protest, journalist, and policing incidents.
Independent evidence that AMLO strengthened courts, the INE, INAI, or other checks is still weak compared with the evidence of media hostility and electoral-pressure attempts.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on self-enrichment, hidden ownership, or preferential benefit remains thin, and several items are still allegations or self-reports.
Independent audit-level evidence on on-time, on-budget delivery and the causal split between AMLO policy and external tailwinds is still incomplete.
